newsitem.title: GREECE: NEW ATHENS AIRPORT 17PCT COMPLETE, AHEAD OF SCHEDULE.
newsitem.headline: NEW ATHENS AIRPORT 17PCT COMPLETE, AHEAD OF SCHEDULE.

text.p: Works at the 658 billion drachmas ($2.4 billion) new Athens airport at Spata are at full swing, with 17 percent of the project completed and ahead of schedule, Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis said on Tuesday.
"The overall progress of works is positive and absolutely satisfactory," Laliotis told reporters during a visit at the construction site northeast of Athens.
"In fact, works are well ahead of schedule which raises no doubts the February 2001 deadline will be met."
Laliotis said that 45 percent of earth-moving works had been completed and about 90 percent of total construction facilities were in place.

The Athens Airport consortium, building the airport is led by Hochtief AG with a 36.125 percent stake, ABB Calor Emag Schaltanlagen AG, 5.0 percent, and Krantz KTK GmbH 3.75 percent. The Greek State holds a 55 percent share in the consortium.
The consortium will operate the terminal which will replace Athens' congested Hellinikon airport for 30 years before ownership is reverted to the Greek State.
The project is one of the largest currently carried out in Europe and is scheduled to be completed in February 2001.
The project is mainly funded by the European Investment Bank with 312 billion drachmas, followed by a syndicate of commercial banks, 98 billion. The Greek state will pay most of the remainder.
Greek sub-contractors were cutting a fair slice in the deal.
"So far, we have sub-contracted 40 percent of all awardable works and Greek firms claim a 95 percent share of this," said the consortium's project site manager George Page.
No precise figures were given over the size of sub-contracted works.
The main airport terminal will have an annual capacity of 16 million passengers and 220,000 tons of cargo at its initial phase of operation.
Laliotis said the project will create directly 7,000 new jobs by the time it becomes operational, as well as an estimated 14,000 jobs indirectly. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
